public_rationale: The evidence does not establish the joint trend as stated. Qwen reports comparable capability with fewer active parameters, while Stanford documents falling per-token prices at specified capability levels. Neither result settles the size and full task cost of representative successive models during the reasoning-model shift. Calling the claim true would require missing comparisons; calling it false solely from smaller models or cheaper tokens would also overreach.
limitations: The observation window and cost measure require interpretation.
One model family cannot establish a market-wide trend.
Per-token price declines are not equivalent to lower application bills.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is an ongoing trend across leading general-purpose models, rather than a claim that every release is larger and dearer.
Bigger ordinarily means parameter count; total and active parameters must be distinguished.
Because the surrounding passage discusses inference and explicitly rejects per-token comparisons alone, more expensive is read as higher cost to run comparable application tasks.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence across representative releases shows that either model size or task-level inference cost is flat or falling, contrary to the asserted general trend.
